rationale: Navigation fix after the negative control: the parent question's discriminator mentioned both store shapes and a snapshot cadence that never leaves a committed entry between the last snapshot and the recovered commit index. The cadence half is now measured in both directions (the control shows the gap absent when the snapshot covers the change), so the discriminator keeps only what remains unmeasured — stores other than the in-memory ones used here, in particular commit-tracking stores backed by production storage. No evidence, comparison or conclusion changes.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same gap and its consequences appear with commit-tracking log stores backed by production storage rather than the in-memory stores used in every measurement, and whether such a store's staging semantics change when the recovered commit index reaches a configuration entry; the cadence direction is measured in both directions, so what remains is store implementation breadth.
